construct: Screening is more likely to detect diseases that remain in a detectable preclinical state for a long time. Slowly progressive disease is therefore overrepresented among screen-detected cases, while rapidly progressive disease is more likely to become symptomatic between screening intervals. Apparent survival among screen-detected cases can consequently look better even without a true mortality benefit.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Screening preferentially detecting indolent tumors with long detectable preclinical phases is length-time bias.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Lead-time bias also creates apparent longer survival after screening, but it does so through earlier diagnosis of the same disease rather than preferential sampling of slow-growing disease.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The explicit overrepresentation of indolent tumors and interval presentation of aggressive tumors makes length-time bias uniquely correct.
